textRun.content: What If public transportation in the Philippines becomes more efficient, organized, and digitally connected, we can significantly reduce traffic time, uncertainty, and congestion that millions of passengers experience every day

A peer-reviewed study published in Scientific Reports (Nature) analyzed 17 major cities worldwide. It found that public transit was superior or equivalent to private cars for reducing travel time in 94% of the scenarios studied. Its modeled future scenario indicated that replacing private-car trips with public transit could potentially reduce car traffic by approximately two-thirds (~67%) compared with the existing situation.

Global research shows that effective public transportation can significantly reduce road congestion.Studies have found reductions ranging from around 15% in vehicle delay following subway expansion to approximately 48% in total road-network delay in a Melbourne modeling study. A global analysis of 17 major cities further found that a large-scale shift from private cars to public transportation could potentially reduce car traffic by about two-thirds.
Philippine Statistics Authority and the Land Transportation Office recorded 14.6 million registered motor vehicles in 2024, with 13.5 million of these being privately owned.
With more vehicles competing for the same road space, traffic congestion has become a major problem in our cities.

According to TomTom's 2025 Traffic Index, which analyzes traffic data from more than 3.65 trillion kilometers of worldwide trip data, Manila recorded an average congestion level of 57%. A 10-kilometer trip took an average of 31 minutes and 45 seconds, increasing to 43 minutes and 29 seconds during evening rush hour.
These figures show a clear problem: as the number of vehicles increases, our existing road networks are becoming increasingly congested, resulting in longer travel times for Filipinos.

But traffic is more than just a daily inconvenience.
Congestion means people spend more time traveling, vehicles consume more fuel, businesses lose productivity, and commuters have less time for their families and other important activities.
The problem also has a serious safety dimension. The Philippine Statistics Authority recorded
13,125 deaths from land transport accidents in 2023
, the highest number recorded in more than a decade.
And this problem is not limited to Metro Manila. Cities across the Philippines are experiencing growing transportation demands, congestion, and challenges in providing safe and efficient mobility.
But congestion doesn’t start and end on the road. For many commuters, the problem begins even before the bus leaves the terminal.

I’ve experienced it. We’ve all  Most of us experienced it: arriving at a bus terminal early, waiting in line, worrying if we’ll still get our preferred seat, and sometimes not even knowing exactly when we should approach the gate.

And during peak travel periods, when terminals are packed, that line can quickly turn into a struggle. Commuters push, shove, squeeze through crowds, and sometimes even pinch or pull just to move forward and secure a seat.
Our localized commuter survey confirms that this isn’t just an isolated experience.

But what stood out even more was what commuters said they wanted.

100% said they would use a mobile application that guarantees their seat and provides an advanced boarding schedule, while 95.45% believed that an organized digital system could reduce terminal congestion.
But the bigger question is: What if we could solve it without forcing bus operators to completely replace the systems they already use?

Thank you, Ana. That commuter experience is exactly why we built TripSync.
[Trace the journey from left to right.]

TripSync connects boarding into one governed journey: demand planning, accessibility-first seating, clear passenger guidance, and verified boarding through a signed QR pass. The system supports staff; it does not replace their judgment. Staff remain in control.
What you are seeing today is a working prototype using demo or synthetic operational evidence. Our next paid pilot will validate how this connected journey performs in a real terminal.
Good morning, judges. We are TripSync, and we built one connected journey for smarter, more predictable bus travel. Our promise is simple: board smart, travel smarter.
I’m Aaron Jalapon, CEO. With me are John Benedict J. Bongcac, CTO; Hazel Mae B. Fuerzas, CMO; and Ana Mae M. Viduya, CFO. Clyde Abner Valdez is our external faculty adviser.
Hazel will begin with why better public transport matters.

Now I will walk you through how passengers can book on the web app. First, on the landing page just click Find a bus, it will redirect you to passenger’s booking page where you can select a route of your choice from Origin to Destination, as well as the planned travel date. Then just click the Search Tickets button to show available buses on the selected route and date.

Next, available buses will be shown with the displayed fare, departure time and the available seats with priority seats. Priority seats are located close to the door for emergency purposes. Then tap continue to preferences  button from the chosen bus.Then it will bring the passenger to the next step, which is to fill-in the name and contact number. They can either select single booking or group booking for booking that includes 2 or more person. Then we also have the optional seatmate affinity matching feature where you or your group can seat closer to people that have mutual preferences as yours. Such as conversation preferences, Lifestyle and travel context, seatmate compatibility and demographic context. After filling the necessary information just scroll down below and proceed by tapping the recommend group seats
Next the passenger will be redirected to the review of assigned seats. Single booking

"TripSync’s seat allocator immediately assigns optimal seats. Families stay together, accessibility needs are protected, and the system calculates a personalized 15-minute boarding window synchronized with the 10:00 PM departure time to eliminate physical station bottlenecks."

"With one tap, the booking is confirmed! TripSync issues an encrypted digital boarding pass showing the exact synchronized departure and boarding window. A single QR covers the whole party and is cached offline on the phone for instant retrieval."
"Before heading to the terminal, the passenger can download their official pass as an image. At the gate, the transit operator simply scans the QR code for instant offline verification."

Now let us look at the operator’s side. This dashboard brings the seven-day demand forecast, fleet context, and decision controls into one view. Staff can see where demand may rise, check available capacity, then accept, modify, or reject the recommendation.
The principle is important: forecasts inform staff. Staff decide. TripSync gives operators earlier visibility, while responsibility stays with the people running the terminal.

A decision becomes more useful when we learn from what happens next. TripSync preserves the forecast snapshot, records the staff action, and compares it with the actual operational outcome. That evidence is reviewed before any retraining or model change. Because we have not completed a field pilot, this is our planned control loop, not a performance claim.

Our core competency is connecting passenger booking with terminal operations—giving operators early visibility, giving staff simple boarding tools, and giving passengers a guaranteed and more predictable journey

The urgency now is clear: 77.27% of commuters already experience excessive waiting, while 81.82% struggle with seat availability and booking uncertainty during peak periods. TripSync addresses these problems before passengers even reach the terminal.
Slide 13 — TripSync Roadmap: Today to Year 5
[Point to Today, then move across the roadmap.]

Our roadmap is evidence-gated: each stage must earn the next. Today, we have a pre-pilot B2B proposition and a working prototype. Year 1 targets incorporation and privacy readiness, five customer wins, at least one paid pilot, and production hardening with operator data. Year 2 targets standardized onboarding, multi-tenant tools, repeatable integrations, and 15 customers. Year 3 growth to 40 customers is conditional on service quality, cash, and team capacity, alongside payment and ticketing integrations and B2B2C validation.

In Year 4, an optional passenger premium tier proceeds only after willingness-to-pay validation; pricing remains unspecified. In Year 5, we expand across the Philippines before evidence-gated ASEAN entry.
Prototype, pilot, scale, premium, and geographic expansion are separate decisions.

which trips will get crowded before the crowd even forms.

a scalable B2B solution that grows without replacing existing systems.
Because TripSync isn’t just about getting passengers on a bus.
more prepared, more predictable, and more connected.
